tasks.short: Check personnel documents and keep each employee’s AFAS dossier complete and current.

today.trigger: An employee, manager or HR colleague submits a document or changes an existing personnel record.
steps: Find the employee’s AFAS dossier and the relevant document in Outlook, Teams or SharePoint.
Check names, dates, approvals and completeness against the applicable CAO and document requirements.
Enter document details and file the approved version with the correct access restrictions.
Ask for missing information and track the correction to completion.
drudgery: Renaming attachments and copying dates into dossier fields.
Checking the same mandatory fields repeatedly.
Chasing missing approvals and duplicate versions.
today.time_sinks: Finding the authoritative version and resolving incomplete submissions take longer than filing a clean document.

lenses.faster: Document classification, routine extraction and filing disappear from my queue; I check only incomplete or sensitive cases. A planning estimate is 20 minutes falling to 7 minutes per case on average, including review and allocated upkeep; this needs measurement.
lenses.autonomous: An approved intake submission starts extraction, validation and filing for permitted document types. My gate covers conflicting records, uncertain extraction and restricted documents before anything is committed.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give each site’s shift managers a day-one dossier readiness report with missing items and named owners. Demand would grow if preparing it became cheap, especially during seasonal hiring.
lenses.joy: I would miss neither renaming attachments nor checking the same dates twice. I want more time to help employees correct difficult records before errors affect their pay or start date.
lenses.options: For a missing document, I compare obtaining the original, requesting an approved substitute or escalating the case. Showing the consequences of each route can change whether a personnel action proceeds.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward resolving dossier exceptions and improving submission quality across the three sites. I gain authority to accept routine evidence within an approved checklist and return incomplete submissions; handling conflicting evidence makes the work more expert.
reach: Absorb routine certificate evidence checks from the Learning and Development Specialist after learning certificate validity rules, Studytube records and site-specific requirements.

tasks.human_edge: I must recognise when a seemingly routine document contains a grievance, disputed performance account or sensitive personal circumstances, and route it with discretion rather than treating it as ordinary filing.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: one extraction call turns an approved document type into checkable fields; deterministic rules then validate and file it. Restricted documents follow a separate human route.

in_practice.trigger: A document arrives through a controlled personnel intake form.
steps: Use the selected document category and access rules to route restricted material away from model processing.
Extract permitted fields from routine documents and retain their source locations.
Validate employee identity, dates, required approvals and duplicates against AFAS.
File qualifying records automatically; send uncertainty or conflicting evidence to my exception queue.
Record the change and check a sample of completed cases for recurring errors.
in_practice.human_gate: I resolve exceptions before filing; grievances, disputed evaluations and documents containing health details stay with authorised staff.
systems: AFAS Profit dossier and supported integration interface
data_needed: Approved document categories, field mappings and validation rules
Employee identifiers and existing dossier metadata
Current CAO requirements and retention schedule
Document access classifications and source approvals
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS dossier history and a restricted processing register containing source references, validation results and exception outcomes, without copying sensitive document text.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 Jonas can read documents into dossier fields; the digest provides no accuracy rate.
The proposed validation rules, restricted-document routing and time saving are design assumptions requiring a local pilot.

risks: A document is attached to the wrong employee or overwrites an authoritative version.
Grievance, performance or health information reaches an inappropriate model or recipient.
Different CAO requirements are reduced to one incorrect checklist.
research_questions: Which AFAS version, dossier features and supported write interfaces are available at Noordhaven?
What proportion of submissions are routine documents that can safely follow one extraction schema?
Can a representative pilot achieve acceptable field accuracy and lower total handling time after exception review?

tasks.short: Keep employee details accurate in AFAS and resolve differences between source records.

today.trigger: An employee submits a change or an approved source system supplies new employee data.
steps: Collect the change and confirm the employee identifier and authorised source.
Compare it with AFAS and check the effective date.
Enter the approved fields, preserving payroll and personnel access boundaries.
Check the result and resolve discrepancies with the employee, manager or Payroll Specialist.
drudgery: Re-keying structured changes already approved elsewhere.
Comparing spreadsheets with AFAS field by field.
Correcting inconsistent identifiers and date formats.
today.time_sinks: Unclear ownership of a field, late changes and differences between sources create repeated checking.

lenses.faster: Approved structured changes flow into AFAS without my copying or comparing them manually. An illustrative average falls from 12 to 3 minutes per change, including exception review and reconciliation; the estimated saving is unvalidated.
lenses.autonomous: An authenticated change request or approved source feed starts deterministic validation and an effective-dated update. I handle source conflicts, unusual changes and protected fields before they can alter the record.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: decide each working day which cross-system discrepancies need correction before the next payroll cut-off. Demand would grow as managers and Payroll see fewer surprises at month end.
lenses.joy: I would miss neither spreadsheet comparisons nor correcting dates entered in the wrong format. I want more time to explain discrepancies and prevent repeat errors at their source.
lenses.options: For a backdated change, I compare permitted effective dates and the payroll consequences supplied by Payroll. That can change whether the case enters the current cycle or waits for a correction cycle.
lenses.altitude: I spend more of my week investigating data conflicts and less entering records. I gain authority to resolve low-risk discrepancies under an agreed source hierarchy, while salary, termination and payroll decisions remain with their authorised owners.
reach: Absorb routine employee master-data reconciliation from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst after learning AFAS field ownership, effective dating and reconciliation controls.

tasks.human_edge: I must question an apparently valid update when it conflicts with what the employee agreed or would create an unfair outcome; a technically consistent record can still be wrong.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: structured data updates need identity checks, source precedence, effective dates and reconciliation, all of which can be written as explicit rules.

in_practice.trigger: An authenticated employee change or approved system feed becomes available.
steps: Match the employee using a stable identifier and verify the source’s authority for each field.
Validate formats, dates, duplicates and payroll cut-off rules.
Apply permitted low-risk updates through a supported AFAS interface.
Route protected fields and conflicting sources to the responsible person without changing them.
Reconcile accepted writes with AFAS and issue a concise exception report.
in_practice.human_gate: I resolve ambiguous identity and source conflicts; Payroll or the authorised HR owner approves changes affecting pay, termination or disputed performance records. Medical reasons are excluded from the feed.
systems: AFAS Profit and supported integration interface
data_needed: Stable employee identifiers and field ownership matrix
Approved source feeds and effective dates
Payroll cut-offs and change permissions
Nonmedical absence fields and permitted termination codes
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS change history and a restricted reconciliation register recording the source, approval reference, previous value, new value and write result.

evidence.claim: Structured validation, effective-dated updates and reconciliation can run through deterministic software without a model.
AFAS Profit 8 supports new-hire data submission through Pocket; this does not establish that Noordhaven has every proposed update interface.

risks: A source conflict is silently resolved in favour of the wrong system.
Backdated updates affect a closed payroll period.
Medical details or unnecessary production and performance data are copied into a general employee feed.
research_questions: Which fields have an agreed authoritative source and can be updated through supported AFAS interfaces?
How many changes require judgement, payroll approval or backdated correction?
Does a pilot reduce total handling time without increasing incorrect or unauthorised updates?

tasks.short: Process approved hires, transfers, promotions, leave changes and departures in AFAS.

today.trigger: HR receives an approved personnel action with an effective date.
steps: Collect the approved action, supporting documents and effective date.
Check contract terms, CAO coverage and required signatures.
Update the employee’s AFAS records and prepare the standard documents.
Notify Payroll and other responsible teams and check that required follow-up is complete.
drudgery: Entering the same effective date in several places.
Building standard letters from an existing approved action.
Sending and chasing routine hand-off messages.
today.time_sinks: Incomplete approvals, conflicting effective dates and missed hand-offs delay otherwise standard personnel actions.

lenses.faster: A complete approved action creates the record changes, standard documents and hand-offs together. My estimated average falls from 30 to 9 minutes per action, including review, exceptions and workflow upkeep.
lenses.autonomous: The workflow starts only after an authorised personnel action is approved. Standard actions run automatically within recorded permissions; conflicting dates, nonstandard terms and departures requiring individual review stop at a human gate.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give site managers a forward view of approved staffing changes and unresolved dependencies before each weekly roster meeting. Demand would grow if managers could obtain it without asking HR to compile a spreadsheet.
lenses.joy: I would miss neither copying approved terms into letters nor asking whether another team received my email. I want more time to prevent a transfer or departure from going wrong for the employee.
lenses.options: For an approved transfer, I compare feasible start dates against Payroll cut-offs, certificate validity and the receiving site’s readiness. The comparison can change the implementation date agreed with the manager and employee.
lenses.altitude: My week becomes a review of personnel actions at risk of missing their agreed date. I gain authority to release complete standard actions and return incomplete requests, with greater expertise in CAO application and effective dating.
reach: Absorb standard personnel-action preparation from the HR Business Partner after learning approval limits, CAO clauses and when employment-law advice is needed.

tasks.human_edge: I must recognise when a transfer, leave arrangement or departure has a disputed meaning or unusual personal consequences and involve the HR Business Partner before implementing it.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: approved action types can map to fixed checks, templates, record updates and hand-offs without model-generated decisions.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised approver releases a complete personnel-action form.
steps: Check action type, approval authority, CAO, effective date and supporting evidence.
Generate the proposed field changes and documents from approved templates.
Execute permitted standard actions and route exceptions for individual approval.
Create tracked hand-offs for Payroll, the manager and other relevant teams.
Reconcile the final AFAS record with the approved action and close completed dependencies.
in_practice.human_gate: The employment decision is approved before the workflow starts; nonstandard terms, disputed cases and termination implementation receive individual review before records or notices change.
systems: AFAS Profit workflows and supported interfaces
data_needed: Approved personnel action and approval authority
Action-specific CAO rules and templates
Effective-date and payroll cut-off rules
Dependency owners and completion evidence
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history with approval references, template versions, effective dates and linked hand-off completion records.

evidence.claim: Approved personnel actions can be implemented using fixed workflows, templates and validation rules; the proposed AFAS configuration is unverified.
SixFifty offers employment-document drafting and related actions within strict workflows; its US legal content cannot supply Dutch CAO rules.

risks: A technically complete action lacks valid approval or uses the wrong CAO.
One system changes while a dependent hand-off fails.
An automated departure workflow sends notices or removes access before the agreed time.
research_questions: What share of actions fit existing approved templates without legal interpretation?
Can AFAS changes and downstream hand-offs be reconciled reliably after partial failures?
Which actions require individual approval even when all fields pass validation?

tasks.short: Check applications against agreed requirements and prepare evidence for the recruiter’s review.

today.trigger: A candidate applies to a vacancy in Recruitee.
steps: Read the application and vacancy requirements.
Check stated experience, availability and required certificates or other eligibility evidence.
Record relevant evidence and identify missing or ambiguous information.
Discuss the application with the Recruiter and record the human decision.
drudgery: Finding the same basic facts in differently formatted CVs.
Copying evidence into candidate notes.
Drafting repeated requests for missing information.
today.time_sinks: Ambiguous CVs and inconsistent vacancy criteria make evidence checking slow and can lead to repeated recruiter review.

lenses.faster: A draft evidence table replaces my first pass of searching and copying, but I still read the application and assess every proposed finding. An illustrative average falls from 20 to 13 minutes, including verification and recruiter discussion.
lenses.autonomous: A new application can start a draft summary against published criteria. I verify it before it enters the decision record, and the Recruiter decides progression or rejection without automatic ranking.
lenses.ambitious: New service: offer warehouse applicants with transferable experience a human-reviewed route to a Recruiter and L&D discussion about training. Demand would grow if preparing this route became cheaper, but training places and recruiter capacity would constrain it.
lenses.joy: I would miss neither copying CV facts nor writing the same clarification email. I want more time to understand candidates whose experience does not fit a standard CV.
lenses.options: I compare direct eligibility, clarification and a permitted training route using the same published requirements. These alternatives can change whether a candidate receives a recruiter conversation instead of an early rejection.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward checking evidence quality and discussing ambiguous applications with recruiters. I gain authority to request factual clarification under agreed criteria, while selection remains with authorised hiring staff; the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter’s factual application-completeness checks after learning structured assessment, qualification evidence and recruitment bias controls.

tasks.human_edge: I must recognise transferable experience, challenge misleading summaries and judge ambiguity in conversation with the candidate and Recruiter; the model cannot decide someone’s suitability.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the person leads application review because summaries can affect employment access, and meaningful human judgement must remain throughout.

in_practice.trigger: A candidate application arrives for a vacancy with approved assessment criteria.
steps: Retrieve only the candidate’s submitted evidence and the vacancy’s published requirements.
Draft a criterion-by-criterion table with source excerpts and explicit unknowns, without scores or ranking.
Read the application and correct omissions, unsupported inferences and irrelevant personal information.
Approve any factual clarification request and pass the verified evidence to the Recruiter.
Record the human progression or rejection decision and its job-related reasons.
in_practice.human_gate: I verify the evidence before use; the Recruiter or authorised hiring manager makes each selection decision. No automatic rejection, personality inference or emotion analysis is permitted.
systems: Approved model service with agreed data handling
data_needed: Published job-related requirements and accepted equivalents
Candidate-submitted application documents
Human assessment and decision reasons
Applicant privacy notice, retention rules and model-service terms
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee’s restricted candidate record, retaining verified evidence, human decisions and the criteria version under the applicant retention schedule.

evidence.claim: GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; a human must meaningfully decide applicant outcomes.
The EU AI Act identifies recruitment and applicant evaluation uses in Annex III; the proposed tool needs classification and applicable-date review before deployment.
Recruitment summaries can create a lasting record of inappropriate or sensitive material.
Evidence extraction may shorten factual review, but the proposed saving has no local measurement.

risks: A summary omits evidence or turns missing information into a negative judgement.
Human reviewers accept the draft mechanically, making oversight ineffective.
Criteria disadvantage protected groups or use proxies unrelated to the job.
Candidate information is retained or shared beyond its stated purpose.
research_questions: Does a blind comparison show that assisted reviews preserve relevant evidence and treat equivalent applications consistently?
Can reviewers demonstrate independent judgement rather than accepting draft conclusions?
What EU AI Act classification, implementation dates and obligations apply to the exact proposed use?
Does verified review time fall enough to justify the additional governance and checking?

tasks.short: Answer employee questions about pay, benefits, leave, training and HR procedures.

today.trigger: An employee or manager contacts HR through Outlook, Teams, telephone or a site visit.
steps: Clarify the question and verify identity where personal information is involved.
Find the relevant CAO, policy, course requirement or AFAS entitlement.
Check which rule applies to the employee’s contract, site and effective date.
Answer the question or refer it to Payroll, the HR Business Partner or L&D.
drudgery: Searching for the current policy link.
Repeating standard explanations.
Forwarding questions without enough context.
today.time_sinks: Finding the right rule and waiting for a specialist answer create repeated contacts, especially outside office hours.

lenses.faster: Approved policy answers and exact entitlement lookups handle routine questions, while a complete ticket replaces my initial investigation for exceptions. An estimated 10 minutes of HR handling falls to 4 minutes per question across the mix, including content upkeep and escalations.
lenses.autonomous: An employee question starts identity checking, fixed retrieval, an authorised lookup where needed and an answer-or-ticket workflow. Ambiguous rules, disputed entitlements and sensitive situations reach a person before substantive advice is given.
lenses.ambitious: New group served: night-shift employees at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo receive routine HR answers while office HR is closed. Demand would probably grow as previously unasked questions become easy to raise.
lenses.joy: I would miss neither hunting for policy links nor repeating standard leave explanations. I want more time for people facing confusing payslips, family difficulties or a disagreement about their treatment.
lenses.options: For a leave question, I can show permitted combinations of leave types and dates using exact balances and approved rules. Seeing these alternatives can change the arrangement the employee asks their manager to approve.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward resolving difficult questions and correcting the content behind repeated contacts. I gain authority to publish approved procedural explanations and route cases directly to the right specialist; interpreting exceptions requires more expertise.
reach: Absorb routine payslip explanation from the Payroll Specialist after learning payslip components and escalation boundaries, while Payroll retains calculations and corrections.
Absorb basic course-eligibility questions from the Learning and Development Specialist after learning Studytube requirements and booking rules.

tasks.human_edge: I must hear when a factual question is really a grievance, financial distress or concern about illness, and offer a confidential human conversation with the right colleague.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: a fixed retrieve-and-answer workflow uses one model step to explain approved content; personal balances and amounts come from deterministic lookups, and unsupported questions become tickets.

in_practice.trigger: An employee opens the approved HR question channel and submits a question.
steps: Disclose AI use, authenticate personal queries and offer a direct human route.
Retrieve current approved content matching CAO, contract and site; fetch personal entitlements through authorised deterministic lookups.
Produce a short answer with source links and exact returned values, without calculating or inventing entitlements.
Escalate unsupported, disputed or sensitive questions with the minimum necessary context.
Review unanswered topics and update approved content with its named owner.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine supported answers can be sent automatically; a person handles disputes, conflicting sources, payroll corrections and sensitive cases. Required works council consent and privacy controls precede launch.
systems: Teams and an approved shift-accessible employee channel
data_needed: Versioned CAO and policy content with named owners
Authorised contract, site and entitlement fields
Escalation rules and specialist queue ownership
Identity, access and conversation-retention rules
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted HR service register containing source versions, resolution status and escalations; personal question histories are retained only where necessary and approved.

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina documents personalised HR answers and escalation to an existing ticket queue; it provides no hours-returned figure.
The Danish study found modest overall work-hour savings from chatbot use, so a local workflow pilot is needed before accepting the task-level estimate.
Article 50 sets disclosure requirements for systems interacting directly with people.
WOR Article 27 consent rights cover relevant personnel-data arrangements and employee monitoring provisions.

risks: An answer uses the wrong CAO, outdated policy or another employee’s entitlement.
Employees cannot authenticate from warehouse or night-shift devices.
Question histories expose health information or become a tool for monitoring employees.
Easier access increases demand enough to offset some released handling time.
research_questions: What share of actual questions can be answered from current approved content or an exact AFAS lookup?
Can warehouse and night-shift employees access the service securely without a company laptop?
What works council consent, privacy assessment and retention design are required for the proposed channel?
Does a pilot reduce total HR handling after content maintenance, repeat contacts and increased demand?

tasks.short: Turn an approved hiring decision into a signed contract and a ready first week.

today.trigger: The Recruiter and authorised manager approve the candidate and offer terms.
steps: Collect approved terms and the new hire’s required personal details.
Prepare the contract and check CAO, working hours, pay and start date.
Obtain approval and signatures and create the AFAS employee record.
Arrange onboarding hand-offs with the manager, Payroll and L&D.
Check missing documents and first-week requirements before the start date.
drudgery: Copying approved offer fields into contracts and AFAS.
Sending repeated requests for missing new-hire details.
Rebuilding the same onboarding checklist.
today.time_sinks: Late approvals, incomplete personal data and unconfirmed site arrangements create last-minute work before day one.

lenses.faster: Approved offer data populates the contract and AFAS draft, and a reusable checklist starts the hand-offs. An illustrative 60 minutes falls to 27 minutes per hire, including contract review, exceptions and first-week checks.
lenses.autonomous: A human-approved Recruitee offer starts data collection, template assembly and onboarding tasks. I approve each contract pack before it is sent for signature, and the employment decision remains with the authorised hiring team.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give each hiring manager a first-week readiness plan covering documents, mandatory training and a named workplace contact. Demand would grow if this became inexpensive, particularly for seasonal warehouse intake.
lenses.joy: I would miss neither copying offer details nor chasing a start date across email threads. I want more time to help new starters arrive confident and resolve obstacles before their first shift.
lenses.options: I compare feasible start dates and onboarding sequences against certificate needs, supervisor availability and Payroll cut-offs. This can change the agreed start date or whether training must happen before operational work begins.
lenses.altitude: My week centres on hires at risk of an incomplete first week and on resolving nonstandard contract cases. I gain authority to release checked standard packs and demand missing readiness evidence, while hiring and pay exceptions stay with their owners.
reach: Absorb onboarding enrolment administration from the Learning and Development Specialist after learning mandatory training sequences, certificate prerequisites and Studytube enrolment controls.

tasks.human_edge: I must check that the contract reflects what the candidate understood and that the manager can provide a safe, workable start; a completed checklist does not prove either.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: approved offers, contract templates, field mappings and onboarding dependencies form a predictable workflow with an individual contract-release gate.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised hiring decision and approved offer terms are recorded in Recruitee.
steps: Transfer approved offer fields and invite the new hire to submit required details through a secure form.
Validate completeness and assemble the applicable approved contract template and AFAS draft.
Present the terms, source approvals and exceptions for my contract-pack review.
After approval, send for signature and activate the agreed AFAS and onboarding steps at the appropriate status.
Track first-week requirements and escalate missing prerequisites to the manager or L&D.
in_practice.human_gate: I approve every contract pack before sending; authorised HR or Payroll staff approve nonstandard terms. The manager confirms operational readiness and qualified staff confirm mandatory training requirements.
systems: AFAS Profit and Pocket where available
data_needed: Approved candidate, vacancy and offer identifiers
Applicable CAO, contract template and authorised pay terms
Required new-hire details and identity-check completion
Start date, site, shift and manager
Mandatory certificates and first-week responsibilities
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee offer history and AFAS onboarding dossier, with contract approval, signature status and linked readiness tasks.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 supports new hires submitting data through Pocket before their first day.
SixFifty demonstrates employment-document and signature workflows, but its US law base does not validate Dutch contract content.
The proposed Recruitee-to-AFAS hand-off, readiness service and time saving require local configuration and measurement.

risks: Incorrect offer mapping produces a contract with the wrong pay, hours or CAO.
New-hire identity or bank details are collected through an insecure channel.
A signed contract is mistaken for permission to begin work without required safety training.
Agency workers are incorrectly placed into the direct-employment contract workflow.
research_questions: Can approved Recruitee offer fields map reliably to Noordhaven’s AFAS onboarding process?
Which contract variants and CAO exceptions require specialist review?
Who can confirm first-week readiness at each site, and is the evidence available before the start date?
Does a pilot improve week-one completion while reducing total administrator handling time?

tasks.short: Find verified employee-file facts for authorised questions and personnel actions.

today.trigger: A manager, HR colleague or employee requests information from a personnel file.
steps: Confirm the requester’s authority and the purpose of the inquiry.
Search AFAS and permitted SharePoint records for relevant evidence.
Compare dates and versions and identify missing or conflicting information.
Provide the minimum necessary facts with sources or escalate an unresolved conflict.
systems: Studytube where certificate evidence is needed
drudgery: Opening multiple files to locate one date or clause.
Copying source references into replies.
Rechecking which document version is current.
today.time_sinks: Poor indexing, conflicting versions and unclear requester permissions make simple inquiries take several searches.

lenses.faster: Permission-filtered retrieval produces an evidence brief with source locations, removing most searching and copying. An illustrative average falls from 20 to 7 minutes, including checks for ambiguity and allocated index maintenance.
lenses.autonomous: An authorised request starts a fixed lookup and evidence-extraction workflow. Exact approved facts can be returned automatically; conflicting records, restricted material and interpretations await my review.
lenses.ambitious: New service: provide HR Business Partners with a dated evidence brief before a transfer or promotion discussion. Demand would grow if they could obtain reliable facts without asking me to search the file manually.
lenses.joy: I would miss neither opening ten attachments nor copying the same contract date into another email. I want more time to resolve contradictory records and explain what the evidence actually supports.
lenses.options: A brief can distinguish the signed contract, a later approved amendment and an unapproved manager note. Comparing these sources can change whether HR proceeds with an action or first corrects the record.
lenses.altitude: My week moves toward resolving evidence conflicts and checking access boundaries. I gain authority to certify that specified facts match authoritative records, while the HR Business Partner retains decisions about their employment consequences.
reach: Absorb factual case-brief preparation from the HR Business Partner after learning evidence hierarchy, confidentiality and the boundary between a recorded fact and legal interpretation.

tasks.human_edge: I must recognise when the file is incomplete, contested or misleading and refuse to present a convenient summary as an established fact.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: permission checks and retrieval follow fixed rules, while one model step extracts a small, source-linked evidence brief from permitted text.

in_practice.trigger: An authenticated requester submits a permitted personnel-file inquiry with a stated purpose.
steps: Check field-level and document-level permissions before retrieval.
Retrieve authoritative structured fields and only the permitted supporting documents.
Extract the requested facts with source locations, effective dates and explicit conflicts.
Return exact routine facts or route ambiguous and restricted cases for my review.
Record access and the evidence version used without creating an unrestricted copy of the dossier.
in_practice.human_gate: I approve interpretations and conflict resolution; health records, grievances and sensitive performance material stay outside routine model retrieval and follow their restricted handling process.
data_needed: Requester identity, role and permitted purpose
Document permissions and authoritative-source hierarchy
Employee identifiers and document effective dates
Approved categories of questions and restricted-record exclusions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted access register and the relevant AFAS request record, containing requester, purpose, source references and review outcome.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 demonstrates extracting document content into dossier fields; the digest does not establish permission-aware file-question answering in Noordhaven’s environment.
Coca-Cola Andina demonstrates HR answers differentiated by employee context, supporting the feasibility of controlled contextual retrieval rather than this exact dossier workflow.
Source-linked extraction with permission checks is a proposed design; retrieval quality and time savings remain unvalidated.

risks: Retrieval exposes a document the requester could not open directly.
A later amendment or disputed record is missed.
A generated brief converts an allegation into a statement of fact.
A stale index returns superseded evidence for a consequential personnel action.
research_questions: Can retrieval enforce existing permissions before any content enters the model?
Are signed documents, amendments and effective dates indexed well enough to identify authoritative evidence?
Does testing on conflicted files reveal omissions that would make automatic factual replies unsafe?

tasks.short: Collect missing employee records from managers, colleagues and staffing agencies.

today.trigger: A hire, personnel action, training requirement or periodic check reveals missing evidence.
steps: Identify the missing item, its owner and the date it is needed.
Ask the employee, department or staffing agency for the minimum required information.
Track replies and send reminders across email and agency portals.
Check the submission and request corrections where needed.
File accepted evidence and tell the dependent process owner it is ready.
drudgery: Maintaining parallel chase lists.
Sending repeated reminders.
Matching attachments to employees and outstanding requests.
today.time_sinks: Unclear ownership, inaccessible submission channels and agency-portal differences turn a simple request into several contacts.

lenses.faster: A tracked request, secure upload link and fixed reminder schedule replace my chase spreadsheet and most follow-up emails. An illustrative average falls from 15 to 6 minutes of active handling per request, including exception follow-up and maintenance; waiting time is separate.
lenses.autonomous: A missing-item check starts a request to the named owner, validates receipt and sends scheduled reminders. I intervene for disputed requirements, repeated nonresponse, access problems and sensitive submissions.
lenses.ambitious: New group served: flex workers from all three agencies get a clear route for submitting only the evidence Noordhaven genuinely needs. Demand would grow with seasonal intake, while agency agreements and data-minimisation rules limit what we collect.
lenses.joy: I would miss neither chase spreadsheets nor sending a third copy of the same request. I want more time to help people who cannot access a portal or do not understand what evidence is acceptable.
lenses.options: I compare asking the employee, requesting agency confirmation or using an existing verified record. These routes can change who must act and prevent Noordhaven from collecting an unnecessary personal document.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward removing recurring submission barriers and resolving overdue cases before they block a start or transfer. I gain authority to accept listed equivalent evidence and escalate unresolved requests to named owners; complex agency cases require more expertise.
reach: Absorb certificate-evidence chasing from the Learning and Development Specialist after learning acceptable proof, validity periods and Studytube completion rules.
Absorb routine agency onboarding-document coordination from the Recruiter after learning agency responsibilities and data-sharing limits.

tasks.human_edge: I must distinguish unwillingness from an access, language or trust problem and help the person find an acceptable route without unnecessary pressure or disclosure.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: missing-item rules, request ownership, reminders, upload status and escalation deadlines are predictable and do not need an agent.

in_practice.trigger: An approved checklist identifies missing evidence for a named employee or flex-worker assignment.
steps: Check whether valid evidence or sufficient agency confirmation already exists.
Create a request for the minimum required item with an owner, deadline and secure submission route.
Send approved reminders and route portal access failures to my queue.
Validate receipt using structured checks and send ambiguous evidence for review.
File accepted evidence, close duplicate requests and notify the dependent process owner.
in_practice.human_gate: I resolve disputed requirements, equivalent evidence and repeated nonresponse; document collection cannot automatically block employment or operational assignment without the responsible human’s decision.
systems: Microsoft 365 request tracking and secure upload
Agency portals through supported interfaces or human-assisted entry
data_needed: Approved evidence requirements by worker type and site
Agency responsibility and data-sharing agreements
Request owners, contact preferences and deadlines
Existing evidence status and accepted equivalents
Retention rules and restricted-document routing
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS checklist or restricted flex-worker request register, recording item status, request owner, reminders, evidence reference and exception decisions.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 supports pre-start data submission through Pocket, providing a product example of structured employee intake.
SAP describes HR agents that nudge stalled approvals; this supports reminder feasibility but does not establish an AFAS or agency-portal integration.
A deterministic request tracker can replace repeated manual chasing; the proposed time saving depends on submission quality and channel access.

risks: Noordhaven collects documents that should remain with the staffing agency.
Reminders reach the wrong person or continue after valid evidence is received.
Workers without suitable devices or language support cannot complete the request.
Unsupported portal automation fails silently or creates duplicate submissions.
research_questions: For each agency, which evidence must Noordhaven hold and which can be satisfied by agency confirmation?
Do the portals provide supported interfaces, or must their steps remain human-assisted?
What proportion of follow-up is caused by missing information versus access, language or unclear requirements?
Does the workflow reduce active handling without increasing duplicate requests or worker complaints?

role.altitude: I become the coordinator of reliable personnel transactions and accessible HR information across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. My week focuses on exceptions, readiness and source quality, with authority to release standard actions, accept approved equivalent evidence and return incomplete requests.
reach: From the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: routine employee-data reconciliation, after learning source ownership, effective dates and AFAS integration controls.
From the HR Business Partner: factual personnel-case briefs and standard action preparation, after learning confidentiality, evidence hierarchy and escalation boundaries.
From the Learning and Development Specialist: certificate-evidence checks and onboarding enrolment administration, after learning mandatory training requirements and Studytube controls.
From the Recruiter: application-completeness checks and agency document coordination, after learning structured assessment and agency data-sharing responsibilities.
From the Payroll Specialist: routine payslip explanations using approved content, after learning pay components and correction boundaries.
role.ceiling_note: The listed tasks total 728 hours per FTE annually. Applying the task estimates gives about 444 hours per FTE, or 889 hours across both posts, of possible capacity; overlapping workflows, implementation work and new demand must be deducted before treating this as available time. Hiring decisions, medical assessment, disputed employment matters and payroll approval remain with authorised specialists.
skills_to_grow: Apply both CAOs to routine administrative cases and recognise exceptions.
Configure and monitor AFAS workflows, permissions, effective dates and reconciliations.
Maintain clear, versioned HR guidance with named specialist approvers.
Check model extraction against source evidence and recognise unsupported conclusions.
Handle AVG/GDPR access, minimisation, retention and sensitive-data boundaries.
Work with the works council on relevant personnel-data arrangements and understand applicable EU AI Act duties.
Support shift workers and flex workers through accessible submission and question channels.
Measure end-to-end handling time, error rates, day-one dossier readiness and week-one onboarding completion.
role.ambitious_version: I run a three-site HR readiness service that identifies missing evidence and unresolved hand-offs before they disrupt a hire, transfer or first week. Together with Recruiters, managers and L&D, I use those findings to improve week-one completion and investigate preventable 90-day departures, while leaving candidate selection and performance judgement with people.
